LibreMaps has no account, no ads and no analytics. It only talks to these open services, and only when you use the feature:

• Map tiles and fonts: OpenFreeMap (tiles.openfreemap.org) sees the map area you view.
• Search: Photon by Komoot (photon.komoot.io) sees what you type.
• Routes for walk, bike and car: FOSSGIS Valhalla (valhalla1.openstreetmap.de) sees your start and end points.
• Public transport: Transitous (api.transitous.org) sees your start and end points.
• Places nearby (Food, Coffee, Fuel and the other shortcuts): an Overpass server and Photon (or Nominatim at openstreetmap.org if Photon finds nothing) see the area you search.
• Place details (opening hours, phone): Nominatim at openstreetmap.org (or an Overpass server if it has nothing) sees the name and area of the place you open. For fuel stations in Spain, prices and hours come from the Ministry for Ecological Transition (sedeaplicaciones.minetur.gob.es), which is asked for a whole province at a time and so only sees the province.
• Speed limits: Valhalla sees your position while you drive, if Road alerts is on.
• Offline maps: OpenFreeMap (tiles.openfreemap.org) sees the areas you save, and Nominatim at openstreetmap.org sees the centre of each one, to give it a name. Without internet, search, nearby places and routes come from your saved areas on the phone.
• Speed cameras: an Overpass server (overpass.kumi.systems, maps.mail.ru or overpass-api.de) sees the outline of your route, if Road alerts is on.
• Approximate position when GPS has no fix: ipwho.is sees your IP address, if that option is on.
• Official traffic incidents in Spain: the DGT's open data feed (nap.dgt.es) is downloaded whole, so it learns nothing about where you are, if Traffic alerts is on.
• Reports by other drivers: the Nostr relays relay.damus.io, nos.lol, relay.primal.net and offchain.pub see the area you're looking at or driving through, if Traffic alerts is on. A report you send is public: it holds the spot, your direction and the time, signed with a one-use key so your reports can't be linked to each other. Like every server listed here, the relays see your IP address.

Road alerts and the approximate position can be switched off in Preferences. Your last known position is stored only on the phone.

Outside Spain, fuel prices and official traffic incidents come from each country's open data:

• France: fuel prices from prix-carburants (data.economie.gouv.fr), asked about the area of about 10 km that the station you open is in. Official incidents on national roads from Bison Futé (tipi.bison-fute.gouv.fr), downloaded whole, if Traffic alerts is on.
• Germany: official motorway incidents from the Autobahn API (verkehr.autobahn.de), which is asked only about the motorways near your route, if Traffic alerts is on.
• Italy (MIMIT, mimit.gov.it), Portugal (DGEG, precoscombustiveis.dgeg.gov.pt) and Mexico (Comisión Nacional de Energía, publicacionexterna.azurewebsites.net): fuel prices from national files downloaded whole, so they learn nothing about where you are.
• Austria: fuel prices from E-Control (api.e-control.at), asked about the area of about 1 km around the station. By law it only publishes the cheaper stations, so the others show no prices.
• Slovenia: fuel prices from goriva.si, asked about the area of about 5 km around the station.

Fuel prices are only looked up when you open a fuel station.
